links.comparator_used: Conventional (default) probability threshold, compared with a Youden Index-optimized cut-off of 0.23, on the same models
links.outcome: Specificity and balanced accuracy for COVID-19 mortality prediction
links.effect: Specificity rose from 29.0% to 82.3%; balanced accuracy rose from 61.1% to 65.6% at the 0.23 cut-off
links.tradeoff: The conventional threshold gave high sensitivity but poor specificity. The abstract gives no numbers for the sensitivity change at the optimized cut-off, so any sensitivity loss is not quantified. The balanced accuracy gain was modest, and the Youden Index is a statistical criterion rather than one based on clinical costs.
links.quote: The ideal cut-off discovered by threshold optimization was 0.23, raising specificity from 29.0% to 82.3% and balanced accuracy from 61.1% to 65.6%.
